summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Incomplete Dominance occurs when the F1 hybrid displays an intermediate phenotype between parental extremes (e.g. Snapdragon flower color). The F2 phenotypic ratio matches the genotypic ratio: 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White (1:2:1). Co-dominance occurs when both alleles express equally and simultaneously in the heterozygote (e.g. ABO Blood Group IA IB expressing both Antigen A and Antigen B).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 3.1 Incomplete Dominance (Snapdragon & 4 O'Clock Plant)
- **Cross**: True-breeding red-flowered (*Antirrhinum majus* / Snapdragon or *Mirabilis jalapa*) and white-flowered plants yield **pink-flowered** $F_1$ hybrids ($Rr$).

$$F_1 \text{ Selfing } (Rr \times Rr) \longrightarrow F_2 \text{ Phenotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{1:2:1} \text{ (1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White)}$$

$$F_2 \text{ Genotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{1:2:1} \text{ (1 } RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr)$$

- **Key Takeaway**: In incomplete dominance, the **Phenotypic Ratio matches the Genotypic Ratio (1:2:1)**, overriding the classical Mendelian $3:1$ ratio.

### 3.2 Co-dominance Mechanics
- In co-dominance, there is no intermediate blending; **both alleles of a heterozygote express their respective gene products simultaneously and with equal strength**.
- *Example*: Human $I^A I^B$ blood group heterozygotes have RBCs presenting both Antigen A ($\text{N}$-acetylgalactosamine) and Antigen B (galactose) on their surfaces.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Molecular Basis of Incomplete Dominance
conceptBreakdown.title: Molecular Basis of Incomplete Dominance
conceptBreakdown.content: In Antirrhinum, the R allele encodes a functional anthocyanin pigment synthase enzyme; homozygous RR produces 100% pigment (Red), heterozygous Rr produces 50% pigment (Pink), and rr produces 0% pigment (White).

conceptBreakdown.heading: MN Blood Group System
conceptBreakdown.title: MN Blood Group System
conceptBreakdown.content: Human MN blood grouping exhibits pure co-dominance: LM and LN alleles produce M and N glycoprotein antigens; heterozygotes (LM LN) express both antigens without dominance or recessiveness.
